content.text:
Traced the whole flow: `createPlayer.ts:47` builds the invite link as `/api/footy/auth/verify/player-invite/{token}?redirect=/footy/auth/claim`. The route (`route.ts:22-23`) calls `claimPlayerInvitationCore`, which validates the token server-side and returns `{name, email, token}` — that whole object gets appended as query params on the redirect to the claim page. So the page never does its own lookup today; it just trusts the query string, and `ClaimSignup.tsx:92-95` re-derives an "invalid" state at runtime from whatever's missing.

Two things fall out of that:

**The security framing doesn't hold up.** The token isn't actually hidden by the indirection — `claimPlayerInvitationCore` returns `token` unchanged and it's appended right back onto the claim page's URL (`?name=...&email=...&token=...`). So going through the API route buys you no secrecy benefit over linking straight to the page; the token sits in the browser bar and history either way. Drop that as a reason to keep it.

**What the indirection actually buys is shared plumbing across three purposes.** `player-invite`, `extra-email`, and `enquiry` all reuse the same route for: origin-checked redirect building (`buildURLWithParams` in `api.ts:132`, preventing open redirects), and consistent Sentry tagging/error capture (`route.ts:39-49`). `extra-email` redirects to `/footy/profile`, `enquiry` redirects to an arbitrary caller-supplied URL — neither of those targets "unpacks" a token the way you're proposing claim should. If you special-case `player-invite` to do its own server-side lookup on the page, you end up with two different patterns for the same "email link → verify token → land somewhere" shape, for no benefit since the thing you were trying to gain (hiding the token) isn't real.

There's also a live bug worth fixing regardless of which way you go: the route catches invitation errors and redirects with a specific `error=` message (e.g. "Invitation has expired"), but `ClaimSignup` never reads that param — it silently falls back to a generic "Missing or invalid invitation details." for every failure mode. That's independent of the indirection question and worth fixing either way.

My take: keep the shared verify route for consistency with the other two purposes, but fix the dropped `error` param so specific failure reasons actually reach the user, and consider having `ClaimSignup`'s props reflect that error state explicitly (e.g. `{ status: 'ok', name, email, token } | { status: 'error', message }`) rather than re-deriving validity from optional strings. That gets you the "required, well-typed props" benefit you're after without duplicating the redirect-safety/observability logic that's currently shared across three call sites.

'use server';

import { deliverContactEnquiryCore, sendEnquiryCore } from '@/lib/core/sendEnquiry';
import { EnquirySchema } from '@/types/actions/SendEnquiry';

/**
 * Validate and initiate an enquiry verification flow.
 *
 * Validates the provided rawData against EnquirySchema, creates a verification
 * token, persists an email verification record and a pending contact enquiry
 * tied to that token, constructs a verification URL (including the provided
 * redirectUrl as a URL-encoded `redirect` query parameter), and sends a
 * confirmation email containing the link.
 *
 * @param rawData - Unvalidated enquiry payload. Expected to match the shape
 * enforced by EnquirySchema; parsing will throw if invalid.
 * @param redirectUrl - Destination URL to redirect the user to after successful
 * verification; will be URL-encoded and appended to the verification endpoint.
 * @returns A Promise that resolves once the verification record and contact
 * enquiry are stored and the confirmation email has been sent.
 * @throws {ZodError|Error} If validation (EnquirySchema.parse) fails.
 * @throws {Error} If token creation, persistence via
 * emailVerificationService/contactEnquiryService, or sending the email fails.
 * @remarks
 * - Side effects: persists records via emailVerificationService.create and
 *   contactEnquiryService.create, and sends an email via sendEmail.
 * - The verification link targets:
 *   `${getPublicBaseUrl()}/api/footy/auth/verify/enquiry/{token}?redirect={encodedRedirectUrl}`.
 */
export async function sendEnquiry(rawData: unknown, redirectUrl: string) {
    const data = EnquirySchema.parse(rawData);
    await sendEnquiryCore(data, redirectUrl);
}

/**
 * Deliver a contact enquiry identified by a verification token.
 *
 * Looks up the enquiry by token and throws if none is found. If the enquiry has
 * already been delivered (deliveredAt is set) the function resolves with `{
 * enquiry: 'already-delivered' }` and performs no further actions. Otherwise,
 * it formats the enquiry message, builds an HTML email (subject includes the
 * enquirer's name), sends the email to the configured recipient, marks the
 * verification token as used, and marks the enquiry as delivered.
 *
 * @param token - The verification token associated with the contact enquiry.
 * @returns A promise that resolves to `{ enquiry: 'already-delivered' }` if the
 *          enquiry was already delivered, or `{ enquiry: 'verified' }` after
 *          successful delivery and updates.
 * @throws {Error} If no enquiry is found for the provided token.
 */
export async function deliverContactEnquiry(token: string) {
    return await deliverContactEnquiryCore(token);
}

That reasoning holds up. Given no shared plumbing to preserve, here's how each of the three flows actually splits — they're not symmetric, which matters for the plan:

**`player-invite`** has a real destination page already (`/footy/auth/claim`) — this is the clean case. Move the lookup straight into the page as a Server Component: change the route to `/footy/auth/claim/[token]/page.tsx`, call `claimPlayerInvitationCore(token)` there, catch and Sentry-capture the error in the page itself, and render the error UI directly from the caught message — no query param round-trip at all, so the injection concern disappears entirely for this flow. `ClaimSignup` then gets `name`/`email`/`token` as真-required props, no more runtime "is this actually valid" derivation in the client component.

**`extra-email`** and **`enquiry`** are structurally different: their redirect targets (`/footy/profile`, an arbitrary caller-supplied URL) aren't pages that own or unpack a token — they're just "land somewhere after the side effect runs." There's no page to move the lookup into; the side effect (mark verified, deliver the enquiry) has to happen on the GET itself. So "self-contained" for these two means splitting the one generic `[purpose]/[token]` route into two dedicated thin route handlers — `verify/extra-email/[token]/route.ts` and `verify/enquiry/[token]/route.ts` — each calling its own core function and repeating the Sentry capture, as you said is fine.

For the `?error=` problem specifically: since the destination pages for these two aren't part of the verification flow, you can't just drop the query param — but you can close the injection hole by replacing free text with a closed status code (`?status=expired|used|not-found|ok`) and having each destination map codes to fixed copy, never rendering the query value verbatim.

104	export class AppError<TCode extends AppErrorCode = AppErrorCode, TDetails = unknown> extends Error {

124	     *

126	     */

128	        super(init.message, { cause: init.cause });
129	        this.name = new.target.name;
130	        this.code = init.code;
131	        this.expected = init.expected ?? true;
132	        this.details = init.details;

286	 *
287	 * Handles various error types and converts them to appropriate AppError subclasses:
288	 * - AppError instances are returned as-is
289	 * - ZodError instances are converted to ValidationError
290	 * - Standard Error instances are converted to InternalError
291	 * - Non-Error values are wrapped in InternalError
292	 *
293	 * @template TDetails - The type of additional error details
294	 * @param error - The unknown error value to normalize
295	 * @param options - Configuration options for error normalization
296	 * @param options.message - Custom error message to use instead of the original
297	 * @param options.details - Additional details to attach to the normalized error
298	 * @param options.publicMessage - Public-facing message safe to display to users
299	 * @returns A normalized AppError instance with consistent structure and properties
300	 */
301	export const normalizeUnknownError = <TDetails = unknown>(
302	    error: unknown,
303	    options: NormalizeUnknownErrorOptions<TDetails> = {},
304	): AppError => {
305	    if (error instanceof AppError) {
306	        return error as AppError<AppErrorCode, unknown>;
307	    }
308	
309	    if (error instanceof ZodError) {
310	        return new ValidationError(
311	            options.message ?? 'Validation failed.',
312	            {
313	                cause: error,
314	                details: options.details,
315	                publicMessage: options.publicMessage,
316	            },
317	        );
318	    }
319	
320	    if (error instanceof Error) {
321	        return new InternalError(
322	            options.message ?? error.message,
323	            {
324	                cause: error,
325	                details: options.details,
326	                publicMessage: options.publicMessage,
327	            },
328	        );
329	    }
330	
331	    return new InternalError(
332	        options.message ?? 'Non-Error value thrown.',
333	        {
334	            cause: error,
335	            details: options.details,
336	            publicMessage: options.publicMessage,
337	        },
338	    );

354	 * - {@link AppError}: defer to its `expected` flag.

360	 */

362	    if (error instanceof AppError) {
363	        return error.expected;
364	    }
365	
366	    if (error instanceof ZodError) {
367	        return true;
368	    }
369	
370	    return false;

391	    }
392	
393	    if (error instanceof ZodError) {

`player-invite` is done — all changes are unstaged and ready for you to review/commit. Summary:

- `claim` page moved to `/footy/auth/claim/[token]/page.tsx` (Server Component); it calls `claimPlayerInvitation(token)` directly, catches/Sentry-captures the error itself, and renders a specific, server-derived `publicMessage` (no query-string round-trip, nothing attacker-controllable).
- `claimPlayerInvitationCore`'s errors now carry deliberate `publicMessage`s ("This invitation has expired.", "already been used.", etc.) instead of generic AppError defaults — this is the specific-error-text fix that was previously getting silently dropped.
- `ClaimSignup` no longer re-derives an "invalid invitation" state client-side; props are trusted as valid since the page guarantees it before rendering.
- `addPlayerInviteCore` now links straight to `/footy/auth/claim/{token}`.
- The shared `verify/[purpose]/[token]` route lost the `player-invite` case; `extra-email` and `enquiry` are untouched for now.

Here's the user story for the rest:

---

**Title: Remove shared `/api/footy/auth/verify/[purpose]/[token]` indirection for `extra-email` and `enquiry`**

**As a** developer maintaining the auth verification flows,
**I want** the `extra-email` and `enquiry` email-link verifications to each run through their own dedicated route handler instead of a shared, purpose-switched route,
**so that** verification outcomes are never carried as free-text query parameters that a manipulated URL could forge, and each flow's error handling is self-contained (matching the change already made for `player-invite`).

**Background / rationale:**
The current `verify/[purpose]/[token]/route.ts` redirects to a caller-supplied URL with either the purpose's return data or `?error=<free text>` appended. Because the destination pages (`/footy/profile`, an arbitrary `redirectUrl`) don't own the token and can't re-derive validity themselves, they must trust that query string — including `error`, which is attacker-forgeable by anyone who edits the URL. This was already fixed for `player-invite` by moving the token lookup server-side into the page that owns it; `extra-email` and `enquiry` have no such dedicated page, so they need their own fix shape.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Split the route into two dedicated handlers: `src/app/api/footy/auth/verify/extra-email/[token]/route.ts` and `src/app/api/footy/auth/verify/enquiry/[token]/route.ts`. Delete the generic `[purpose]/[token]` route once both are moved.
- [ ] Each handler calls its own core function (`verifyEmailCore`, `deliverContactEnquiryCore`) directly — no shared purpose switch.
- [ ] Each handler repeats its own Sentry `captureUnexpectedError` call with purpose-specific tags (`action`, `route`) — accepted duplication, not factored back into shared code.
- [ ] Replace the free-text `?error=` query param with a small closed enum (e.g. `?status=expired|used|not-found|ok`) that the destination page maps to fixed, hardcoded copy — the destination must never render the query value as display text.
- [ ] `verifyEmailCore`'s and `deliverContactEnquiryCore`'s thrown errors get explicit `publicMessage`s (mirroring the `claimPlayerInvitationCore` change) so the status-code mapping has real per-case text to draw from.
- [ ] Update `requestPlayerEmailVerification` (`verifyEmail.ts:115`) and `sendEnquiryCore` (`sendEnquiry.ts:69-72`) to build links against the new dedicated routes.
- [ ] Update/replace `route.vitest.spec.ts` with two focused spec files; update any spec asserting on the old `?error=` shape.
- [ ] Confirm `/footy/profile` and whatever `enquiry` redirect targets exist read the new status enum (if they display anything at all) rather than the old raw error text.

content.text:
Before writing the story: this is a real, existing inconsistency, not a hypothetical. Across the 13 forms using Mantine `useForm`, only two (`SignIn.tsx:164`, `ClaimSignup.tsx:144`) disable submit via `!form.isValid()`. The rest — `DeleteAccountForm`, `PlayerProfileForm`, `NewPlayerForm`, `EnquiryForm`, `MoreGamesForm`, `InvoiceForm`, `NewGameForm`, `ForgottenPasswordForm` — leave submit enabled and rely on Mantine surfacing field errors when clicked. Two more are disabled on unrelated conditions rather than validation: `GameInvitationResponseForm.tsx:212` (`!isFormDirty`) and `MoneyForm.tsx:218` (selection count / in-flight state).

My recommendation: standardize on **always-enabled + validate-on-submit**, not disable-until-valid. Reasons:
- It's already the majority pattern (8 of 13 forms), so standardizing this way touches fewer files.
- Disable-until-valid gives no feedback on *why* — a freshly-opened form with `validateInputOnBlur` shows a grayed-out button with zero visible errors until the user blurs every field, which reads as broken, not as guidance.
- Validate-on-submit is the accessible default: clicking always does something, errors anchor to the specific fields, screen readers get the standard error-announcement path Mantine's already wired for.

The tradeoff you're giving up: disable-until-valid does stop wasted submit attempts on forms with expensive submit side effects. That's a reasonable exception, not the rule — worth calling out in the story rather than deciding globally.

**Title: Standardize submit-button disabling behaviour across all forms**

**As a** user filling in any form in the app,
**I want** submit buttons to behave the same way everywhere,
**so that** I don't have to relearn why a button is or isn't clickable on each different page.

**Background / rationale:**
13 components use Mantine `useForm`. Only `SignIn` and `ClaimSignup` disable submit via `disabled={!form.isValid()}`; the rest leave submit enabled and show field errors on click. `GameInvitationResponseForm` and `MoneyForm` disable submit for unrelated reasons (dirty-tracking, selection count) that should stay as-is since they're not validation gates. This split means the same gesture — clicking a grayed-out vs. active button — means different things depending which page you're on.

**Decision to make and record:** adopt **always-enabled submit + validate-on-submit** (with existing `validateInputOnBlur` inline errors left in place) as the project standard, matching the current majority pattern and CLAUDE.md's Mantine-first conventions. Document the decision (e.g. as a short note in `CLAUDE.md`'s UI & Forms section) so it isn't re-litigated per PR.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Remove `disabled={!form.isValid()}` from `SignIn.tsx:164` and `ClaimSignup.tsx:144`; confirm both still show inline field errors on blur/submit and that submitting an invalid form is a no-op (Mantine's `form.onSubmit` already blocks the handler and populates errors when invalid — verify this, don't just delete the prop).
- [ ] Audit the remaining forms (`DeleteAccountForm`, `PlayerProfileForm`, `NewPlayerForm`, `EnquiryForm`, `MoreGamesForm`, `InvoiceForm`, `NewGameForm`, `ForgottenPasswordForm`) for any other validation-gating I've missed (e.g. conditional rendering instead of `disabled`) and bring them in line.
- [ ] Leave `GameInvitationResponseForm.tsx:212` (`!isFormDirty`) and `MoneyForm.tsx:218` (selection count / in-flight) untouched — confirm in the PR description that these are intentionally excluded because they're gating on state other than field validity.
- [ ] Add a one-line note to `CLAUDE.md` under "UI & Forms" recording the standard, so new forms default to it without a repeat discussion.
- [ ] Update/remove any existing tests asserting the old `disabled` behaviour for `SignIn` and `ClaimSignup` (e.g. `ClaimSignup.vitest.spec.tsx`'s "disables the Create login button until passwords are valid" test).
